//: Markup-fidelity fixture for the SETTINGS-PANEL — the floating `.pa-settings-panel` block (keen `PureAdmin.Components.SettingsPanel.settings_panel/1`, svelte `layout/SettingsPanel.svelte`). SCOPE = CONTAINER + STATE CLASS ONLY, with ZERO strict-compare scenarios. This is the rare fixed-chrome LEAF component: it takes NO content slot and emits a large, FIXED internal tree (toggle + content + title + ~13 sections of selects/checkboxes/hint + a reset button). Unlike list/accent-grid (container + a plain-text slot that both wrappers echo identically → a shared golden), there is NO slot here and NO single core-blessed inner shape the comparator could diff: the inner markup is genuinely framework-divergent by DESIGN, and the demo's own inner markup (demo/views/partials/settings-panel.mustache) differs from BOTH wrappers too (the demo uses pa-checkbox/pa-checkbox__box inside the checkbox group; BOTH wrappers instead use the SCSS-blessed pa-settings-panel__checkbox + a bare inner <span>, i.e. they agree with each other and with _settings-panel.scss, not with the demo). The wrappers diverge from EACH OTHER in ways that are legitimate, documented API choices — none of which the markup-fidelity (CSS-class) contract governs: (1) keen ALWAYS emits the Theme / Color-Variant / Theme-Mode sections (hidden via inline style, data-section) and hydrates them from /api/themes/manifests via a phx-hook; svelte conditionally OMITS Theme+Variant when no availableThemes are passed and renders a light/dark/auto FALLBACK mode select. (2) keen carries data-setting / data-section / data-reset JS-binding attributes + i18n label text ("Mode"); svelte carries none and hardcoded English ("Theme Mode"). (3) the two search-position option VALUES differ (keen navbar-input/sidebar-input vs svelte navbar-typeahead/sidebar-typeahead) — a JS-behavior string, not a CSS class, and the mustache demo sides with svelte (navbar-typeahead/sidebar-typeahead); flagged below but out of the class-contract scope. Because compare.mjs does WHOLE-FRAGMENT equality (no sub-tree matching) and no shared full-tree golden exists, this fixture carries NO scenarios: compare passes vacuously (0/0) and correctness is asserted structurally — the base pa-settings-panel class + the --open JS state class (cssStateClasses) + every __* element class deferred as acknowledged PROSE (fixed chrome, framework-divergent internals, no sub-component fixture/dumper to fixture-ref). The ONE feature both wrappers would need for even a container-shell golden — a class passthrough — is keen-only (keen has a `class` attr; svelte's SettingsPanel declares no `class` prop and silently drops it), so it is NOT modeled as a shared oracle feature. Capability (axis 1: --open claimed by cssStateClasses, all 9 __* deferred; axis 2: zero shared features, both maps empty) is the completeness proof here.
goldenConventions: No scenarios → no goldens. See the leading note for why a shared full-tree golden is impossible (fixed, slot-less, framework-divergent chrome) and why container-shell class-passthrough is keen-only. Correctness is carried by the structural contract: the base block class, the --open JS state class, and the deferred element-class inventory.

features.//: ZERO shared oracle features. The block has exactly ONE modifier (pa-settings-panel--open), which is JS-toggled at runtime (svelte: an isOpen $state bound with class:; keen: the PureAdminSettings hook), never a prop → it is a cssStateClass, not a feature. There is no slot and no shared prop-driven markup, so there is nothing for a feature→class mapping to assert. The class passthrough that list/accent-grid model as a shared `extraClass` feature is keen-only here (svelte drops an unknown `class` prop), so modeling it would force svelte's map to claim a no-op prop — omitted to keep the contract honest.

cssStateClasses.//: Block modifier(s) in main.css that are NOT feature-driven props — toggled by JS at runtime. Listed so axis-1's reverse check treats them as legitimately unclaimed-by-a-feature.
cssStateClasses.pa-settings-panel--open: panel open/slide-in state — toggled at runtime (svelte isOpen $state via class:pa-settings-panel--open; keen PureAdminSettings JS hook on toggle click + click-outside). Never SSR-authored / prop-driven, so not a feature.

deferred.//: Every __* element class of the pa-settings-panel block. These ARE emitted in SSR markup (not JS-built — so NOT cssStateElements), but they are FIXED internal chrome with no content slot and the two wrappers emit genuinely divergent internals (conditional Theme/Variant/Mode sections, data-setting/data-section attrs, i18n vs hardcoded labels, different option value strings). There is no settings-panel sub-component with its own dumper wiring to fixture-ref (a ref would DEFER?-fail), so each is acknowledged as PROSE — out of the strict-compare surface. The class names themselves all exist in _settings-panel.scss and are emitted identically-named by BOTH wrappers; only their surrounding content/attributes diverge.
deferred.pa-settings-panel__toggle: floating toggle button (both wrappers emit it identically-classed: button.pa-settings-panel__toggle > span.pa-icon.pa-icon--settings)
deferred.pa-settings-panel__section: one settings group; repeated ~13x — count/content differs per wrapper (keen always emits Theme/Variant/Mode; svelte gates them)
deferred.pa-settings-panel__label: section label (<label>/<span>) — text is i18n in keen, hardcoded EN in svelte
deferred.pa-settings-panel__hint: small helper text under a select
deferred.pa-settings-panel__checkbox-group: flex column wrapping the checkbox rows
deferred.pa-settings-panel__checkbox: a checkbox row (label.pa-settings-panel__checkbox > input + span) — BOTH wrappers use this SCSS-blessed class; the demo mustache instead uses pa-checkbox here
